strategic_differentiation: This MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship proposal differentiates on two interlocking planes within the single-researcher, single-beneficiary MSCA-PF evaluation frame. First, at the research level: the project targets the single empty cell in a systematic literature review's research-gap matrix — Real-Time Decision Support × PlanetScope — and claims a deliberately narrow, defensible novelty: no prior work couples learned multimodal fusion with explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation and economically optimised irrigation decision-making end-to-end for row crops. The distinguishing posture is the honest, end-to-end uncertainty chain carried from multi-sensor observation through probabilistic diagnosis to profit-maximising counterfactual decision, argued against specific precedents (Bayesian Maximum Entropy, copula-based scheduling, dynamic Bayesian networks, MF-FusionNet) that each address part of the chain but not all three stages together. The edge is not 'using satellites for irrigation' but the integrity of uncertainty propagation across the full chain. Second, at the methodological risk management level: the design is risk-managed by construction through two interchangeable diagnostic routes — a rigorous one-step probabilistic fusion route (Route A, direct probabilistic fusion via Bayesian hierarchical model or Gaussian process) and a lighter homogeneous-patch proxy route (Route B, sidesteps the sub-pixel resolution problem) — sharing one decision engine, so no single methodological failure can halt the research programme. Objectives are measurable against a defined validation protocol (uncertainty calibration: whether 90% prediction intervals contain truth ~90% of the time; decision quality) rather than asserted. At the researcher and hosting level, differentiation derives from a genuine two-way knowledge transfer: the fellow brings the peer-reviewed uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration method to ELTE's environmental-modelling group, and takes up the host's geoinformatics and field-validation competences in return — a knowledge exchange evidenced by specific deliverables (methods seminars, co-supervised MSc thesis) rather than asserted generically. Open-science commitments (open validation data and protocol, open research software, FAIR data management) are integral to the research design and serve the validation transparency argument, not merely compliance.
